nodes.label: Clipboard poll dedup bypassed on the sensitive path
nodes.norm_label: clipboard poll dedup bypassed on the sensitive path
nodes.summary: In the Linux polling monitor, `last_hash` is the only dedup marker and it is assigned at the end of the accepted path, after the `is_sensitive_content` check. The sensitive branch `continue`s before reaching it, so a rejected value never advances the marker and the same bytes are re-read, re-scanned and re-logged on every 500 ms tick. Cadence measured at mean 505.0 ms against `Duration::from_millis(500)`, every interval >=502 ms. The invariant 'process each distinct value once' was enforced by code placement, so any early return above the dedup silently opted out.

nodes.label: Rejecting content counts as having handled it for the dedup marker
nodes.norm_label: rejection counts as handled for the dedup marker
nodes.summary: The stated reason the sensitive path must advance the marker: the whole point of the dedup is 'we already handled this exact clipboard content', and rejecting is handling it. The original code treats rejection as 'not handled', which is why the loop never settles. Advancing the marker on rejection removes duplicate reporting without weakening the guarantee -- the check stays unconditional, sensitive content still never reaches SQLite, and the log line still interpolates nothing.

nodes.label: Extract a pure seam before you can test an untestable loop
nodes.norm_label: extract a pure seam before you can test an untestable loop
nodes.summary: The polling loop was uncallable from a test: infinite `loop`, `thread::sleep`, live `arboard` clipboard. The fix was therefore larger than a three-line reorder, because the tick decision first had to be extracted into a pure OS-free function (`classify_polled_text`, returning Unchanged / RejectedSensitive / Capture) that owns the hash compare, the marker advance and the sensitive check -- the exact ordering under test. The OS work (`capture_html_content`, classify, DB insert) stays in the loop, on the Capture arm only.

nodes.label: Log flood rate is bounded by how long a secret sits in the clipboard
nodes.norm_label: log flood rate is bounded by how long a secret sits in the clipboard
nodes.summary: A subagent reported the line repeats forever, ~172,800/day. The parent checked the on-disk log and that is wrong: SESSION_START/SESSION_END markers bound the burst to 2 lines/sec for as long as a secret sits in the clipboard. pid 46505 produced 1 sensitive line and stayed alive 37 s more; pid 75553 produced 17 lines over 9.6 s and the app then ran 65 s longer, heartbeating, before a clean tray-quit. The 62-minute gap needs no special explanation either -- only the 10 s evdev heartbeat is present, so the clipboard was not holding flagged content while the thread polled the whole time.

nodes.label: RED test written against the seam in its pre-fix ordering
nodes.norm_label: red test written against the seam in its pre fix ordering
nodes.summary: The fixed ordering was written into the new seam first, and that was wrong: TDD needs RED. The seam was reset to preserve the current buggy ordering (sensitive check first, then hash compare and assign) so the test failed for the intended reason -- tick 1 returns RejectedSensitive, tick 2 must return Unchanged, and on the old ordering tick 2 also returns RejectedSensitive because the marker never advanced. RED was exit 100, then GREEN exit 0. Three tests: dedup across ticks, a different secret is still rejected (guards against dedup being repurposed as suppression), and sensitive content is never Capture.

nodes.label: A stale known-failure note in AGENTS.md misleads a future session
nodes.norm_label: stale known failure note in agents md misleads a future session
nodes.summary: AGENTS.md documented `commands::updater_cmds::tests::the_user_agent_reports_the_target_selected_release_version` as a known pre-existing nextest failure. It passes now (21/21 in scope, green in the full run) because the test became `#[tokio::test]` with `sent_user_agent` binding a real loopback TcpListener instead of depending on another test leaking a default Tokio handle. Measured 2026-10-01 on vps-bcb: 3275 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped, so a red --lib run now means a real regression. The note was rewritten to record the fix rather than deleted, and the debt item was closed.

nodes.label: A test that passes on unfixed code proves nothing
nodes.norm_label: a test that passes on unfixed code proves nothing
nodes.summary: The ROTATE-02 test seeded the log already over the cap, so the original open-time size check caught it and the test passed on the unfixed code -- a useless test. It was caught only by reconstructing a RED variant (original code plus new tests) and running that, and the technique is now recorded as the standard: a test never seen to fail is not evidence. The rewritten test crosses the cap through write_entry only, and is genuinely RED. The same session also caught a self-deadlock in the same change -- rotate_logs re-locking active_file inside its own guard, on a non-reentrant Mutex -- before compiling.

nodes.label: 'Cannot affect my run' is not the same as 'safe to discard'
nodes.norm_label: cannot affect my run is not the same as safe to discard
nodes.summary: A cleanup `git checkout --` on the VPS reverted two `snipset-cli` files that were not this session's. The reasoning was that the drift was in a different crate and so could not affect the test run -- a false inference, and the correct cleanup was to stash, not revert. Nothing was lost: the VPS copies duplicated the same author's own already-pushed commit `2ff5df447`, and the VPS was restored to that commit with a clean tree. The same inference was then explicitly refused a second time on the push, where four foreign files (a Snipset workflow file and three ai-skills files) were left uncommitted and reported instead.

nodes.label: Linux has no single-instance implementation at all
nodes.norm_label: linux has no single instance implementation at all
nodes.summary: On Linux `is_primary_instance` is hardcoded true -- the only false assignment sits inside `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]` -- and `initialize_core_services()` runs at lib.rs:322, about 77 lines before the Tauri single-instance plugin registers at :399, so a second launch opens the DB and spawns a duplicate clipboard poll thread. The module itself is entirely `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]`, a named Win32 mutex: there is no Linux implementation and no libc/fs2/flock dependency or existing file-locking code in the crate. Documented only, left to the user, with three options (new flock dep, reorder to use the plugin callback, accept as debt).

nodes.label: gh 2.102.0 removed gh issue edit --state
nodes.norm_label: gh 2.102.0 removed gh issue edit state
nodes.summary: Reused id. Independently hit from a different note: plan-issue-sync.mjs:270,278 used `gh issue edit --state`, and gh 2.102.0 (2026-09-30) removed the flag in favour of dedicated `gh issue close`/`reopen`, so issue #441 was stuck open with a stale Approved body. Its two tests had been asserting the broken behaviour, so script and tests moved together (40/40, then 423/423) and the fix was proven end-to-end against live GitHub: #441 closed at status Complete. The same mistake class as the earlier --json assumption, where one instance was fixed and the second learned.

nodes.label: Synthetic secret fixtures in a detector test must look real
nodes.norm_label: synthetic secret fixtures in a detector test must look real
nodes.summary: A pre-push secret scan over this session's own diffs returned three hits. All three are deliberate test fixtures for the sensitive-content detector -- a `sk_live_` prefixed token and a fake PEM header -- and they must be realistic or the detector tests prove nothing, since a fixture that does not resemble a real credential tests the wrong thing. Classified as fixtures, not credentials, on that basis rather than by suppressing the scanner.

nodes.label: A green reachability test whose glob never matched the new hub
nodes.summary: Reused id. `90 - System/Audits/index.md` is a real hub with an inbound wikilink from `90 - System/index.md`, but it matched neither pinned hub shape, so the reachability test passed with a real hub at zero coverage -- precisely the failure the test exists to prevent, because `vault_lint.scan_vault`'s orphan filter exempts any file named `index.md` and therefore structurally cannot report an unreachable hub page. The test is genuinely the only detector, which a teeth test asserts directly with a positive control so the fixture cannot pass for the wrong reason.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-26 - widen-vault-reachability-scope [ses_f217dd475ffezDFQEpyyNO5Hnf].md:L42] Widen the glob, not the expected-hub list

nodes.label: Explicit exclusion rather than relying on accidental glob depth
nodes.norm_label: explicit exclusion instead of relying on glob depth
nodes.summary: `90 - System/Legacy/Restricted Sources/index.md` sits three levels below `90 - System` (four path parts), so `90 - System/*/index.md` cannot match it -- verified by globbing, not assumed, and pinned by a test asserting the depth. But leaving it an accident of glob depth was refused, because the directory is protected and requiring reachability there could produce a failure nobody is permitted to fix. `EXCLUDED_HUB_PREFIXES = ("90 - System/Legacy/",)` makes the exclusion explicit, commented, and non-dead: five tests cover it, including one proving the rule still fires under a hypothetical `**` glob.

nodes.label: A widened shape must be seen red under a mutant
nodes.norm_label: widened shape must be seen red under a mutant
nodes.summary: Nine new tests were added, then evidence was produced rather than assumed: narrowing `SYSTEM_HUB_GLOB` to a non-matching pattern, subprocess-isolated, gives 7 RED / 9 GREEN under the mutant and 0 RED / 16 GREEN real. The seven that go red are the real glob-teeth; the nine that stay green are glob-independent by design (positive control, linter-blindness proof, leaf-exclusion guard, set-vanished direction) and are explicitly not counted as widening-teeth. One test was initially filtered out by a name mismatch ('discovers' rather than 'widened_shape') and the filter was corrected rather than the count reported as complete.
